24.verdict: level with the channel's earlier Shorts at this age: 799 views against a median of 873 (0.9x)

worked: High viewer satisfaction: likes_per_100 reached 3.3, outperforming every benchmark short in the cohort (which ranged from 1.3 to 2.8), showing the core story of an autonomous probe hack resonated strongly with those who stayed.
hurt: Slow narrative momentum throttled distribution, leaving views_per_hour at 27.0 and total views at 799 compared to the cohort median (~44 views_per_hour and ~1,200 views), caused by delaying the central conflict until beat 5 while beats 2 through 4 lingered on technical backstory.
diagnosis.change_next: Move the crisis immediately to beat 2 by starting with 'Deep Space 1 lost its navigation system millions of miles out, leaving it totally blind' rather than spending three beats on NASA backstory and engine specs before introducing the problem.

72.verdict: level with the channel's earlier Shorts at this age: 1012 views against a median of 1019 (1.0x)

worked: High algorithmic test reach with a feed share of 0.941, showing the algorithm pushed the Short directly into feeds.
Strong viewer sentiment among those who finished, earning 2.7 likes per 100 views compared to the median ~2.2 of earlier uploads.
hurt: Steep drop in mid-video retention down to a watching_at_50 of 0.639 (vs. 0.77-0.85 on top performers), dragging avg_viewed to 69.72% due to three beats of backstory/specs before the actual conflict.
Initial retention at watching_at_5 was mediocre at 1.295 (compared to 1.40-1.58 on stronger shorts), indicating the hook phrasing did not immediately compel repeat loops or instant holds.
diagnosis.change_next: Move the inciting incident straight to beat 2: after the hook, immediately introduce the failure ('Millions of miles from Earth, its navigation eye shut down completely') instead of spending three beats on tech specs before the crisis.
